gloss: whisky and water; a drink diluted with water

definitions.gloss: whisky and water; a drink diluted with water
definitions.explanation: An alcoholic drink, typically whisky or shochu, mixed with water. One of the most common ways to drink spirits in Japan.

examples.japanese: ウイスキーの{水割|みずわ}りをください。
examples.english: I'll have a whisky and water, please.

examples.japanese: {焼酎|しょうちゅう}は{水割|みずわ}りで{飲|の}むのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like to drink shochu diluted with water.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}には、{氷|こおり}をたっぷり{入|い}れた{水割|みずわ}りが{格別|かくべつ}においしい。
examples.english: On a hot day, a water-diluted drink with plenty of ice is exceptionally delicious.

notes:
USAGE:
{水割|みずわ}り is formed from {水|みず} (water) + {割|わ}る (to dilute). The pattern ～{割|わ}り is used for various dilution methods: {炭酸|たんさん}{割|わ}り (with soda water), お{湯割|ゆわ}り (with hot water).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ウイスキーの{水割|みずわ}り (whisky and water)
- {焼酎|しょうちゅう}の{水割|みずわ}り (shochu with water)
- {水割|みずわ}りを{作|つく}る (to make a mizuwari)

CULTURE:
In Japan, {水割|みずわ}り is one of the standard ways to order spirits at bars and izakaya, alongside ロック (on the rocks), ストレート (neat), and お{湯割|ゆわ}り (with hot water).
